The 256 was an internal contradiction inside that same document, so narrowing it to 200 reconciled the document with a bound it already stated canonically; it introduced no new business rule.
tools/validate_pack.py PASSES. The control system itself is intact; every gate failure below is a repository-integration failure, not a defective control package.

verify_repo_integration.py reports 7 MISSING_PROJECT errors. The repository was never bootstrapped into the control system: it has no architecture/ adopted governance, no tests/ projects, and its module assemblies (UnicoreCRM.Crm, .Operations, .Sales, .Platform, .Workflows, .ApiHost) do not match the layered layout (UnicoreCRM.Domain/.Application/.Infrastructure/.Api) that the shipped gate definitions and wire_architecture_tests.py assume.

Making the architecture and contract gates executable requires an adopted gate registry at backend/architecture/gate-registry.json. That path is hard-denied by protected_write_patterns(), is not in machineManagedRuntimePaths, and an untracked architecture/ directory fails working_tree_clean(). It therefore cannot live in this task's diff range and cannot stay uncommitted: it must be committed before identity.baseCommit, which rebases the implementation subject and invalidates the ff5047f binding of every recorded evidence row.

The canonical trusted-evidence path is repo-integration/github-actions.unicorecrm-ai-gates.yml.example. Its trust model requires the control plane checked out from a separate protected immutable ref (UNICORECRM_CONTROL_REPOSITORY/UNICORECRM_CONTROL_REF), a repository secret UNICORECRM_CI_ATTESTATION_KEY, and a passing 'verify_repo_integration --execute' step. None of the three exists: .unicore-ai is a local unversioned directory, no secret is configured, and repo integration fails.

Seven maintained suites plus npm run api:check were rerun against ff5047f and all pass; they are recorded as diagnostics, not governance evidence, because run_and_record_evidence.py is disabled by design. Only the build gate has a genuine governance evidence row, at trust level LOCAL.

gaps.statement: No repository-wide architecture gate exists. The registry gate names tests/UnicoreCRM.ArchitectureTests, which does not exist; the canonical wiring tool generates a project referencing UnicoreCRM.Domain/.Application/.Infrastructure/.Api, none of which exist here. The only real architecture assertions in the repository are Lead-specific and embedded in verify-lead-nurture-qualification.ps1, which must not be promoted to a general gate.

No backend contract gate exists. The registry gate names tests/UnicoreCRM.ContractTests, which does not exist. The repository's real contract mechanism is npm run api:check in frontend/unicorecrm-web, which run_gate.py can only execute from the backend repo root and which binds to content-hashed, uncommitted frontend artifacts rather than to the backend subject.

Closing G-ARCH-GATE and G-CONTRACT-GATE requires committing adopted governance under backend/architecture/, which rebases the implementation subject off ff5047f. Task 10C is forbidden from doing this and must report IMMUTABLE_SUBJECT_REBIND_REQUIRED.

The four edges this slice needs (Workflows.Atomic.Application -> Leads/Contacts/Tasks Contracts, Leads.Application -> Products.Contracts) are frozen as REQUIRED participants by lead-contact-qualification-authority.md section 10.2 but were never transcribed into the allowlist. Recording them is reserved to an approved architecture decision.

The operation's admitted taxonomy has no correctly classified retriable internal-contention code: only RATE_LIMITED and INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE are catalogued retryable:true and neither describes this condition. No canonical authority makes resolving this a freeze precondition.
